video_title: Biggest Offseason Questions With HUGE Impact Across The NBA: Giannis, LeBron, Top Pick & More

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst on the importance of celebrating NBA championships
quotes.excerpt: it's so hard to win a championship that I highly encourage celebrating the ever-living hell out of it.
quotes.quote: You guys know one of my things is it's so hard to win a championship that I highly encourage celebrating the ever-living hell out of it. And I know that people in the NBA don't really are not going to really listen to me, but I always encourage it. So I want to see for these next three to five weeks, I want to see this trophy on the back of Mitchell Robinson's pickup truck. I want to see it God knows where Josh Hart and Jalen Brunson are going to take it. I want to see these guys at parties. I want to see them enjoying every little bit of it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The likelihood of Giannis Antetokounmpo being traded before the NBA draft
quotes.excerpt: if/when he gets traded, it will reshape the entire league, maybe, there's a decent chance of reshaping the entire league

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: If/when he gets traded, it will reshape the entire league, maybe, there's a decent chance of reshaping the entire league and change the balance of power and be a massive story. And wherever he goes, if he's healthy, will be almost certainly a contender.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: This all goes back to the comments from Jimmy Haslam six weeks ago, right? When they introduced Taylor Jenkins and he said we're either going to trade Giannis by the day the draft arrives or we're going to pivot to building around Giannis and we're going to have him around. And so, one way or the other, it's Tuesday afternoon right now, by a week and change from now, we're going to have the answer, one way or the other.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat's long-term interest in trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: Miami has had interest in Giannis for months. They have talked to the Bucks about this on and off

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Miami has had interest in Giannis for months. They have talked to the Bucks about this on and off for months. I know that the word offer is being thrown around out there in some places. I am not going to throw around the word offer because the word offer is sacred in the NBA. But I think we can say with certainty that there are concepts of an offer.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Can I clarify that slightly? They don't love it, I would say, right? Because if they loved it, they would have done it. They might end up making a trade with the Heat, but if there was a trade where they felt great about it, and they were like, yeah, we got to do it, they it would be done by now because the Heat have been interested for months.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Miami Heat's trade assets and the Andrew Wiggins contract situation
quotes.excerpt: Andrew Wiggins has a player option for $30 million that he is almost certain to pick up.
quotes.quote: They are not trading Bam Adebayo, okay? But everybody else on the roster, you could probably assume that the Heat would be willing to have some level of conversation with. The interesting thing is that Andrew Wiggins has a player option for $30 million that he is almost certain to pick up. But they can't trade him until he picks it up. So if Andrew Wiggins does not want to be traded in this deal, he could sit there and just keep his mouth shut until the last second of his player option. They can't trade him. If he does pick up his player option, then that $30 million expiring contract they could trade him.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brown's contract status and his value to the Boston Celtics
quotes.excerpt: Jalen Brown is a different player than Tyler Herro. He's under contract for three more years at a gigantic number.
quotes.quote: Jalen Brown is a different player than Tyler Herro. He's under contract for three more years at a gigantic number. It's something like $180 or $190 million. It's over $60 million a year. A bonafide star player under contract control. This is a massive decision that you'd have to make about trading these two guys that have gone to one finals and then won another finals.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Mazzulla's coaching style and its impact on the Boston Celtics
quotes.excerpt: Joe Mazzulla is dogmatic about the way he wants to play basketball, arguably dogmatic to a fault.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Joe Mazzulla is dogmatic about the way he wants to play basketball, arguably dogmatic to a fault, although he did win coach of the year this year.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: I would I would not say arguably.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of trading for Giannis Antetokounmpo on the Boston Celtics' system
quotes.excerpt: Trading for Giannis, regardless of who you use in the package, fundamentally changes the way the Celtics have to play.
quotes.quote: Trading for Giannis, regardless of who you use in the package, fundamentally changes the way the Celtics have to play. And he's a basketball coach. Good, great basketball coaches change their systems based on their personnel. Of course I think Joe Mazzulla can coach a different way. I'm not saying that if they got Giannis that he wouldn't be, of course he'd be able to coach him. But you're talking about convincing your head coach who is married to this system to divorce himself from that system and do over. That is not just like, oh, Giannis's press conference, we'll see at training camp.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The historical context of the Ricky Davis trade and its lessons
quotes.excerpt: The trade of Ricky Davis, who was the cornerstone, one of the greatest players ever played for the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.quote: The trade of Ricky Davis, who was the cornerstone, one of the greatest players ever played for the Cleveland Cavaliers, in his after nine years, is comparable to the trade of Giannis Antetokounmpo, rather than the fact that Giannis has delivered a championship and Ricky Davis has not. But same type of thing. And the Rams offered packages that had more draft picks in them. And also, like with Giannis, there were offers at the trade deadline during the NFL season that had more draft picks in them. And it was not until the Rams included this, and I'm not an expert on this at all, but this edge rusher, Jared Verse, okay? I ain't doing any analysis, but they traded a guy who was a two-time all-pro for the last two years, and it was then they actually offered packages that had more draft picks in it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The decision-making process within the Cleveland Cavaliers' front office
quotes.excerpt: I'm not sure who gets the final choice on this. I don't know the answer.
quotes.quote: I'm not sure who gets the final choice on this. I don't know the answer. I guess technically because Wes Edens is the governor, might be Wes Edens. But it was Jimmy Haslam who they had come out and make a definitive statement on this. So, do you think about that, that they had a Taylor Jenkins press conference? Now, I'm just going to point out that Jimmy Haslam, two weeks ago or so, maybe it was three weeks ago, as owner of the Cleveland Browns, I've said this before, I have no idea whether this is going to be a thing, but I will just say that the trade of Miles Garrett, who's the cornerstone, one of the greatest players ever played for the Cleveland Browns, in his after nine years, is comparable to the trade of Giannis Antetokounmpo, rather than the fact that Giannis has delivered a championship and Miles Garrett has not.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler's dissatisfaction with Utah Jazz contract negotiations
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler is upset with how the negotiations have gone and he doesn't want to play for the Jazz.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: We have a story in the Athletic yesterday by Sam Amick quoting sources that say Walker Kessler would like to not play with the Jazz. What was the exact line?

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: The short version is Walker Kessler is upset with how the negotiations have gone and he doesn't want to play for the Jazz.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: In other words, we want to be able to sign an offer sheet and you not to match, or you be willing to sign and trade us.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz's aggressive timeline and restricted free agency challenges
quotes.excerpt: Restricted free agency is not a pleasant experience, but we're making a very fair offer.
quotes.quote: That's been the messaging from his camp for a while. They were not thrilled that the Jazz didn't send him to Indiana before the Pacers ended up trading for Avit Zoubats, which by the way, that took away a potential destination. The Wizards trading for Anthony Davis took away a potential destination. The trade deadline didn't help Kessler's positioning. The Jazz's thing is like, listen, we get it, it gets hairy and restricted free agency is not a pleasant experience, but we're making a very fair offer, the most dollars ever given to a big who's never been an All-Star. If you can get a better offer, that's certainly your right, and then it's our right to match, or not, depending on what the offer could be. But that's where it's tougher for a team like the Lakers for example.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Walker Kessler's desire for unrestricted free agency
quotes.excerpt: Walker wants to be allowed to sort of be unrestricted by saying I don't want to be with the Jazz.
quotes.quote: What Walker wants is to basically be allowed to sort of be unrestricted by saying I don't want to be with the Jazz.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Utah Jazz salary cap management and frontcourt commitments
quotes.excerpt: The Jazz have to price in Walker Kessler on their salary sheet and they have to price in Keyonte George.
quotes.quote: The Jazz have to price in Walker Kessler on their salary sheet and they have to price in Keyonte George on their salary sheet, and they owe 100 million dollars a year to their frontcourt, Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Anderson Varejao's long-term agreement with the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs match the offer sheet and two years later Varejao becomes an unrestricted free agent.
quotes.quote: The way the Dan Gilbert, Danny Ferry story ends, the Cavs match the offer sheet and two years later Varejao becomes an unrestricted free agent. And they come to terms after three bloody years, Dan Gilbert and Danny Ferry, two Irishmen to the core. They have come to terms on an agreement for Anderson Varejao after literally years of being at war with each other.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' lack of actual cap space and roster constraints
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers are sitting here with theoretical cap space. The Lakers technically don't have any cap space.
quotes.quote: The Lakers are sitting here with theoretical cap space. The Lakers technically don't have any cap space. None. Because LeBron James has a massive cap hold. Rui Hachimura's cap hold is like 20 something million, and Austin Reaves' cap hold is 21 million. Now the Austin Reaves cap hold is good news, because Austin Reaves will sit on their books at 21 million, even if he agrees to a contract that's twice that. It will still sit on their books at 21 million and they can sign him last and be over the cap and be okay. The LeBron and Hachimura things are a problem.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' urgent need for a defensive anchor
quotes.excerpt: They need a defensive anchor desperately.
quotes.quote: They need a defensive anchor desperately.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' potential trade path for a starting center
quotes.excerpt: Walker Kessler is a defensive anchor. The Lakers have cap space. They could sign him.
quotes.quote: Walker Kessler is a defensive anchor. The Lakers have cap space. They could, knowing that the Jazz have an offer out there of 28-ish million, they could say, here is an offer over the top of that. And they could do that. But we got a couple of problems. They'd have to renounce LeBron and Hachimura to do that, number one, or they'd have to get them into contracts that were pretty small relative to what they were.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Restricted free agency offer sheet timeline constraints
quotes.excerpt: They can't sign an offer sheet until July 6th.
quotes.quote: They can't sign an offer sheet until July 6th. And then once an offer sheet is signed, the team who's got the restricted rights has two days to match it. And if the Lakers don't find out whether or not they're going to get Walker Kessler until July 8th, they won't have anybody left to sign. So there's not going to be an offer sheet. If you want Walker Kessler, the only way you're going to be able to get him is by doing a sign and trade with the Jazz.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' need to prioritize roster upgrades over immediate center acquisition
quotes.excerpt: They need a lot more athleticism, they need a lot more perimeter defense.
quotes.quote: They need a lot more athleticism, they need a lot more perimeter defense. They need a real center. They probably need another ball-handler, even if they bring back Austin Reaves, beyond just him and Luka. They need a lot of stuff. They had a fine year last year, obviously. They got to the second round, won a playoff series, even with their main guys banged up like that. It was an impressive season. On the other hand, they had a no-hope series against Thunder and they are miles behind the Thunder and they are miles behind the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks' successful roster construction and playoff performance
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks were able to have one of the most impressive playoff runs.
quotes.quote: I give the Knicks all the credit in the world because certainly the belief around the league was that it was Thunder and Spurs and there was a drop-off after that. And the Knicks were able to have one of the most impressive playoff runs and finish off the Spurs in five games, despite trailing in double figures in all those games.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' lack of draft assets and roster depth
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers had back-to-back picks at 17 in 23 and 24. They drafted Jaylen Hood-Schifino and Dalton Knecht.
quotes.quote: The Lakers had back-to-back picks at 17 in 23 and 24. They drafted Jaylen Hood-Schifino and Dalton Knecht. Those are two zeros. And if those if they, you know, and they were good players drafted after both of those guys. And when the Hood-Schifino draft, Jaime Jaquez and Brandin Podziemski were both drafted right after Jaylen Hood-Schifino. Like, those guys would be players that would certainly help right now. You go to the year after that, when they drafted Dalton Knecht at 17, I mean, let's see who is I mean, Jacob Walter just was starting for Toronto in the playoffs, Jalen Tyson was drafted after that, Keon Ellis, Keshawn George was drafted after that. Like, they those guys would be players that would certainly help right now. If those two picks had turned into rotation players, you would feel differently about where the Lakers are at. But there's just not a lot of talent currently on the roster.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' history of trading draft picks for established talent
quotes.excerpt: They traded picks for Anthony Davis and they won a championship. That means never having to say you're sorry.
quotes.quote: They traded picks for Anthony Davis and they won a championship. That means never having to say you're sorry. They did a they they made a good pick in 22 with Max Christie in the second round. They traded him. They traded him for Luka Doncic, which you would do for sure.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' lack of draft assets and cap flexibility
quotes.excerpt: They don't have enough assets and salary cap flexibility to get to a place where they can fill them all now.
quotes.quote: They have a lot of holes to fill and I think the goal this summer just has to be to start filling holes wherever they can and then see where they're at and then keep building and filling in from there. Because there's just not enough they don't have enough assets and salary cap flexibility to get to a place where they can fill them all now. So it should just be how can we make the team as good as possible for the next few years this summer and then how do we keep adding to that going forward.

quotes.speaker: Tim McMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James' status as a top-25 player
quotes.excerpt: LeBron James is still a legitimate All-Star. Like he's still a top-25 player in the league.
quotes.quote: LeBron James is still a legitimate All-Star. Like he's still a top-25 player in the league. What you're saying doesn't like I don't think they can do what you're saying and bring LeBron James back next year.

quotes.speaker: Tim Bontemps
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' need to find low-cost talent to build around LeBron
quotes.excerpt: Find players on the margins, find low-cost players that you can develop into guys.
quotes.quote: Find players on the margins, find low-cost players that you can develop into guys. I'm not saying that doesn't mean you can't bring LeBron back, but the whole idea of they just you have to just find as many gains as you can this summer. To Brian's point about the center thing, I don't think they desperately have to go get a center this summer because guess what, if there's not a center that's good enough to be a difference maker this summer, blowing assets on a center to get a center that's not ultimately going to be good enough, to me doesn't make sense.
